fields.features_heading: What a Scope Needs Before Work Starts
fields.features_subheading: Scopes typed up after the meeting miss what the client asked for on site. Describe your process, and Emergent builds the form.
fields.feature_1:
Every line marked in scope or out

Estimators mark each line item in scope or out of scope as they walk the job. The client's copy prints the excluded items under their own heading, apart from the included work.
fields.feature_2:
Questions that fit the type of project

Pick remodel or website work and the form asks what that job needs. A remodel asks for room sizes and finishes, and a website asks how many pages and which ones need new copy.
fields.feature_3:
The client signs the finished scope

Clients sign the scope with a finger on a phone or tablet. The signature is saved with the date and the version they signed, and a copy of the signed scope goes to their email.
fields.feature_4:
Milestones that each carry an owner

Give each milestone a date and an owner. When one runs a set number of days past its date, the app emails the project manager the milestone name, the owner, and the days late.
fields.feature_5:
Change requests linked to the signed scope

A change request names the scope it changes and the hours it adds. Each request sits next to the original scope, and the record shows what was agreed first and what came later.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take to your own repository

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository when scopes need to sit beside an existing project system. Host it where you choose and keep building on it.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Businesses Scope a Job
fields.tab_content_1:
Each line in or out, signed on site

Larchgrove Remodeling no longer types up kitchen scopes at the office. Estimator Alaric Bartram marks 14 line items on a tablet as he walks the room. Three are out of scope, the electrical panel upgrade among them, and those print under Exclusions. Amberlyn Haverstraw signs the scope before he leaves her kitchen.
fields.tab_content_2:
Briefs that top $20,000 go to the founder

A brief that lands at Saffronby Studio carries the client's goals, the pages they want, and the budget. Any brief over $20,000 goes to founder Thisbe Calderwick as a Slack direct message before the team drafts a scope. Gildmore Dental asked for a 12-page site on a $28,000 budget, and Thisbe read the brief first.
fields.tab_content_3:
On day 3 of a late cutover, Lysander gets an email

Ketterwick Freight is moving its warehouses onto a new network, and Juniperline IT scoped it as 4 milestones, each with an owner. The cutover is now 5 days past its date. Any milestone 3 days late emails project manager Lysander Elsworth, and his email named the owner and the open tasks.
fields.tab_content_4:
Barnaby approves 16 added hours or no work starts

At Pennydale Events, each change request points to the signed scope and counts the extra hours. Any change over 10 hours waits for account director Barnaby Quinlow before anyone starts on it. The gala client wants another breakout room, which adds 16 hours, and the request sits in his queue beside the original scope.

faq_heading: Scope of Work Form Template FAQ

plan.angle: The results for this query are downloadable Word, PDF and Google Docs scope of work templates plus form-tool template pages that stop at a list of fields. None shows a scope of work form that does the work after the fields: items marked in or out of scope during a site walk, a large brief held for the owner before the client sees it, milestones that alert the project manager when they slip, and change requests weighed against the signed scope. This page shows that working form at four businesses, with every scope saved to a database the business owns. It gives no legal advice: the contract wording stays with the business and its lawyer.
tab_stories: At Larchgrove Remodeling, estimator Alaric Bartram walks a kitchen with a tablet and marks 14 line items in or out of scope; 3 are out, and homeowner Amberlyn Haverstraw signs the scope on the tablet before he leaves.
At Saffronby Studio, a client brief from Gildmore Dental lists a $28,000 budget; any brief over $20,000 goes to founder Thisbe Calderwick in Slack before a draft scope goes back to the client.
At Juniperline IT, the Ketterwick Freight network move has 4 milestones; the cutover is 5 days past its date, and any milestone 3 days late emails project manager Lysander Elsworth.
At Pennydale Events, a change request against a signed scope adds 16 hours for a second breakout room; any change over 10 hours waits for account director Barnaby Quinlow before work starts.
